players.product: merchant semiconductor photomasks (binary, phase-shift, EUV) and nanoimprint molds (formerly Toppan Photomask; TSE Prime listing Oct 2025; TOPPAN Holdings holds 46.55%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 Results Briefing (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY ending March 2027 results (CFO Seiichi Itoga, briefing remarks): revenue JPY 345 hundred million, up 14.8% YoY and up 3.5% QoQ; operating profit up 25.3% YoY with an operating margin of 21.3%, 1.8 points better YoY on a higher share of advanced products; EBITDA margin 35.4% (+1.6 points). Versus the prior quarter, gross margin fell from 34.8% to 33.2% and operating margin from 22.8% to 21.3% as fixed costs rose (depreciation and maintenance on newly installed equipment, ERP renewal). In US dollars, revenue rose 2.7% and operating profit 12.0% YoY; QoQ revenue +0.8% and operating profit -6.1%. Average rate 160.72 yen; more than half of transactions are in US dollars. Some large customers were hard to win business from, but the broad customer base kept revenue at the prior-quarter level.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue JPY 345 hundred million, +14.8% YoY; operating profit +25.3%, margin 21.3%; EBITDA margin 35.4%; USD revenue +2.7%, operating profit +12.0%

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 Results Briefing (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Sales mix and customers (CFO, briefing remarks and Q&A): by node, Q1 advanced 35%, middle 35%, mature 30% - the advanced share is up about 5 points YoY and drives the margin improvement; by application, logic 89% and memory 11%. Memory's share rose temporarily in Q4 mainly on strong demand from a Chinese customer, settled in Q1, and part of that demand is rising again from Q2. By region, the US, Korea and Europe shares rose QoQ and China stays high; Taiwan's share and revenue fell QoQ because a quality issue arose for some customers - the masks met customer specifications but a usability problem occurred; the cause was identified and fixed by a process change, orders are unaffected, and the shortfall is expected to be recovered from Q2. Market: semiconductor makers with in-house mask shops focus their resources on the most advanced development and production and increasingly outsource the advanced tier one step behind it.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 node mix: advanced 35%, middle 35%, mature 30%; logic 89%, memory 11%

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 Results Briefing (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (CFO): Q1 progress is about 25% of the full-year forecast published in May; helped by the weak yen, results are broadly on plan and the full-year forecast is unchanged. This year is again positioned as an up-front investment period - in Q1 EBITDA exceeded capex, but capex will increase from Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 progress about 25% of the full-year forecast; forecast unchanged

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 Results Briefing (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and Korea (CFO, results briefing Q&A): the current up-front investment is planned to contribute to sales around 2027 to 2028; until then the worldwide maintenance organisation will raise equipment utilisation at every site for stable supply and productivity. Tekscend's production capacity exceeds competitors', which it believes earns customer trust through stable supply (it cannot say all business shifting from competitors comes to it). In Korea, qualification and tape-outs were temporarily delayed by circumstances at a major customer, but the original investment plan is unchanged and demand and customer requirements are firm in recent moves from Q2; the Korea investment is progressing broadly on the original schedule, and a customer request to pull it forward is not ruled out.
quarterly_data.figure: Investment to contribute to sales around 2027 to 2028

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 Results Briefing (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Memory and China (CFO, results briefing Q&A): memory demand is firm - large customers are bringing qualification inquiries and want early delivery, expected to lift results from Q2 to Q3 onward; the demand growth is in DRAM photomasks themselves (not HBM logic dies). In China, localization is intensifying and local makers are starting to use Chinese-made equipment; Tekscend has no current plan to use Chinese photomask manufacturing equipment but will consider it while watching others; it will protect consolidated profit by shifting its China mix toward high-value-added and advanced masks.
